$comment: Curated library of pitch angles the AI generation pipeline draws from. Phrasings use AGENT-LED ON-BEHALF-OF voice (v1.1) — emails are sent by the talent's agency, not the talent themselves. The LLM rewrites tone/context; merge fields with {curly_braces} are substituted at generation time. talent_name is required in nearly every phrasing now. Edit angles freely as the user learns what works. v2 may add per-angle voice_mode overrides for agencies that prefer talent-led messaging.

angles.name: Worked with a direct competitor
angles.description: Talent has proven track record with a brand the contact's brand directly competes with (per the curated brand_competitors.json graph, not just same industry_id). Strongest competitive proof — shows fit AND creates FOMO.
angles.example_phrasing: {talent_name} recently wrapped a campaign with {competitor_brand} — same vertical, similar audience overlap with {target_brand}. The {format} hit {metric} with a {engagement_rate} engagement rate. {target_brand} hasn't worked with someone in {talent_name}'s space yet — happy to share the full audit.
angles.notes: Highest authored strength. Use with care if competitor is a particularly bitter rival — frame as 'proven track record in this space' not 'I left them for you'.

angles.name: Worked with a same-industry brand
angles.description: Talent has worked with a brand in the same industry_id as the target but not in the curated competitor graph. Strong proof of category fit; weaker than direct-competitor angle.
angles.example_phrasing: {talent_name} has done a few campaigns in {industry_display_name} — most recently with {past_brand}. The {format} drove {result}. We think {target_brand}'s {product_line_or_focus} would resonate with {talent_name}'s audience even more.

angles.name: Worked in an adjacent category
angles.description: Talent worked in a category that's tertiary in niche_industry_affinity but not direct. Catches cross-pollination patterns (e.g. fitness creator who's done supplements work).
angles.example_phrasing: {talent_name} works mostly in {primary_niche} but recently expanded into {adjacent_category} with {past_brand}. The crossover audience is exactly the demographic {target_brand} targets.

angles.name: A similar talent has worked with this brand
angles.description: Direct precedent — a similar_talent in our system has a documented past campaign with the target brand. Implicit social proof; positions our talent as a natural follow-on.
angles.example_phrasing: Noticed {similar_talent_handle} partnered with {target_brand} on {campaign_reference}. {talent_name} shares ~{audience_overlap_pct}% audience overlap with them — different content focus, same demographic. Worth a chat about a follow-on campaign with a different angle?

angles.name: Multiple similar talents have worked with this brand
angles.description: ≥3 similar talents have documented campaigns with the target brand. Signals the brand actively buys creator marketing in this lane; our talent positions as differentiated by a specific angle.
angles.example_phrasing: {target_brand} has worked with {similar_talent_count} creators in {talent_name}'s space this year. {talent_name}'s differentiator is {differentiator} — happy to share the case studies and how the approach compares.

angles.name: Similar talent at a competitor brand
angles.description: A similar_talent worked with one of the target brand's competitors (not the target itself). Positions our talent as the obvious next move for the target brand.
angles.example_phrasing: {similar_talent_handle} just did {campaign_type} with {competitor_brand}. We think {target_brand} would benefit from a creator with {talent_name}'s {my_specific_angle_vs_them}.

angles.name: IAB demographic overlap with brand target
angles.description: Strong IAB Demographic segment overlap between talent's audience and the brand's target customer profile. Quantitative, data-backed angle.
angles.example_phrasing: {talent_name}'s audience is {dominant_gender_pct}% {dominant_gender}, {dominant_age_band} in {top_country} — direct match for {target_brand}'s {product_target}. Detailed demo report available.

angles.name: Strong gender skew matching brand target
angles.description: Talent's audience has a strong gender skew (>65%) that matches the brand's primary target demographic.
angles.example_phrasing: {gender_pct}% of {talent_name}'s audience is {gender} — historically your strongest converting segment for {product_category}.

angles.name: Dominant age band matches brand life-stage target
angles.description: Talent's dominant audience age band aligns with the brand's typical life-stage target (e.g. 30-34 dominant → home buyers; 18-24 dominant → first-job demographic).
angles.example_phrasing: {talent_name}'s dominant age band is {age_band} — exactly {target_brand}'s {life_stage_descriptor} demographic.

angles.name: Niche is a primary affinity for the brand's industry
angles.description: The talent's content niche is listed as a primary tier match for the brand's industry in niche_industry_affinity.json. Highest-fidelity content-fit signal.
angles.example_phrasing: {talent_name} is a {niche_display_name} creator — {target_brand}'s {product_line} is directly in {talent_name}'s content sweet spot. Pitching a {proposed_format}.

angles.name: Recent content series directly fits the brand
angles.description: Talent has a specific recent content series (manually tagged or inferred from analytics) that's directly relevant to the brand's product/category. Concrete, evidence-backed fit.
angles.example_phrasing: {talent_name}'s recent {series_name} series hit {series_metrics}. The content focuses on {series_topic} — would naturally feature {target_brand}'s {product}.

angles.name: Brand recently funded
angles.description: Target brand has a recent funding round (Series A-D), typically detected via Brand Discovery Search 15. Signals fresh budget + scaling phase. Time-sensitive.
angles.example_phrasing: Congrats on the {funding_round} — perfect moment to scale your creator program. {talent_name} works in {category} and has done {past_campaigns_short}.

angles.name: Brand recently launched a product
angles.description: Product launch detected via Brand Discovery (Search 15 or 16). Time-sensitive opportunity to tie content to the launch window.
angles.example_phrasing: Saw the {product_name} launch {launch_timeframe} — congrats. {talent_name} would be a strong fit for a {content_piece} tied to your launch window.

angles.name: Brand currently trending on social
angles.description: Target brand surfaced in Brand Discovery Search 16 (last30days) with high engagement signal. Pitch a content amplification.
angles.example_phrasing: Watched the {recent_viral_moment} play out — {talent_name}'s audience is exactly who's loving this. Worth amplifying with a follow-on.

angles.name: Brand expanding into talent's audience market
angles.description: News detected of the brand entering a new geographic market that's one of the talent's top audience countries. Highly targeted geographic-momentum angle.
angles.example_phrasing: Saw {target_brand} is launching in {market_country} — {audience_pct}% of {talent_name}'s audience is there, specifically the {demographic_descriptor} you'd want to reach.

angles.name: Brand recently in trade press / received award
angles.description: Recent press hit (Adweek, PRWeek, Campaign) or award detected for the brand. Light angle — good as a conversation opener, not a primary hook.
angles.example_phrasing: Congratulations on the {press_or_award} — saw the {publication} coverage. {talent_name} could help extend the moment with creator content.

angles.name: Top audience country matches brand's primary market
angles.description: The talent's #1 audience country is in the brand's sells_in_countries list (or brand sells globally). Light-but-present signal.
angles.example_phrasing: You sell in {market_country}; {audience_pct}% of {talent_name}'s audience is there. Particularly strong in {region_or_cities}.

angles.name: Brand HQ matches talent's top audience country
angles.description: The brand is headquartered in the talent's top audience country. Authenticity-leaning angle — local creator, local brand.
angles.example_phrasing: {nationality_adjective} brand, {nationality_adjective} audience. {talent_name} would be a strong fit for your {market_country} creator roster.

angles.name: Champion contact at the brand
angles.description: A contact at the target brand is classified as `champion` (known fan / internal advocate). Major lift — warm intro from inside.
angles.example_phrasing: {champion_name} mentioned you handle {function} — they thought you'd be a good person to chat with about a partnership with {talent_name}.

angles.name: Worked with the brand's agency-of-record before
angles.description: The target brand uses an agency-of-record for creator partnerships AND the talent has prior relationship with that AOR. Gatekeeper-route advantage.
angles.example_phrasing: We worked with {aor_name} on {past_campaign} — they suggested reaching out about adding {talent_name} to your roster.

angles.name: Met at an event
angles.description: Talent and contact attended the same event (manually tagged by the agency). Strong warm-touch — converts to meetings at much higher rates than cold.
angles.example_phrasing: Good to meet you briefly at {event_name} last {event_timeframe}. Following up on {conversation_topic} — wanted to connect about {talent_name}.

angles.name: Brand publicly aligns with talent's values
angles.description: The brand was flagged by Brand Discovery Search 13 as positively aligned with the talent's values_red_lines (e.g. sustainability, body-positive, anti-diet). Authenticity angle.
angles.example_phrasing: Your public commitment to {value_alignment} is exactly why {talent_name}'s audience would respond well. {talent_name}'s content centres on {related_value}.

angles.name: Past relationship eligible for re-engagement
angles.description: Talent worked with this brand before; cool-down has elapsed (Search 1 in Brand Discovery). Highest-converting angle — warm re-engagement beats cold every time.
angles.example_phrasing: Following {talent_name}'s campaign with you in {past_campaign_date} — we hit {past_metric}. New angle to propose for {upcoming_window}.

angles.name: Same contact pitched before with positive history
angles.description: This specific contact was pitched before and either expressed interest or had a positive prior interaction (per pitch_history outcome). Warm continuation.
angles.example_phrasing: Good to circle back, {contact_first_name}. Last time we discussed {previous_topic} with {talent_name} — wanted to share an update.

angles.name: Strong recent post performance
angles.description: Talent has a recent (last 30 days) post that performed notably above their baseline. Specific proof of current momentum.
angles.example_phrasing: {talent_name}'s recent {post_descriptor} hit {view_count} views / {engagement_rate}% ER — strong indicator of how a {target_brand} feature would perform.

angles.name: Documented past-campaign case study available
angles.description: Talent has a previous_brands entry with detailed performance_notes — i.e. a real campaign case study we can share.
angles.example_phrasing: Happy to share the {past_brand} case study — {talent_name} drove {result_metric} over the {campaign_duration} campaign.

angles.name: Seasonal sales window
angles.description: Current quarter aligns with the brand's known sales season (e.g. Mother's Day for jewellery, Black Friday for retail, summer for swimwear).
angles.example_phrasing: With {seasonal_event} in {time_window}, {talent_name}'s audience is actively shopping for {category}. Worth a campaign?

angles.name: Talent has an upcoming launch / event
angles.description: Talent has flagged an upcoming personal launch or event (cookbook drop, product line, milestone post). Pitch a brand to feature.
angles.example_phrasing: {talent_name} is launching {launch_descriptor} in {launch_window} — would be a natural moment to feature {target_brand}'s {product} in the launch content.

angles.name: Tailored creative concept
angles.description: AI generates a specific content idea based on the full (talent, brand, contact) context — not a generic ask. Always available (the AI generates the concept). Strong support angle to pair with a primary hook.
angles.example_phrasing: Concrete idea: {concept_one_liner}. Would feature {target_brand}'s {product} in {content_format} alongside {related_content_theme} — natural fit for {talent_name}'s feed.

angles.name: Brand has a gap in talent's sub-niche
angles.description: Brand hasn't worked with creators in the talent's specific sub-niche (based on creator_program_presence + scanning their past partnerships). Positioning angle.
angles.example_phrasing: Noticed {target_brand} hasn't worked with creators in {sub_niche} — that's exactly {talent_name}'s space.

angles.name: Brand light on a specific content format
angles.description: Brand's recent social content is underweight on a specific format (e.g. light on Reels, no UGC) that the talent excels at.
angles.example_phrasing: {target_brand}'s {format} output has been quieter recently — {talent_name} could fill that gap with {specific_concept}.

angles.name: Talent is genuine customer of the brand
angles.description: Talent has self-identified (or is verifiably tagged) as a brand customer. Authenticity hook — natural creator-brand alignment.
angles.example_phrasing: {talent_name} has been a customer of {target_brand} for {customer_duration} — worth formalizing the relationship. Their audience already knows they use {product}.

angles.name: Specific deliverable + price ask (buyer role)
angles.description: Default closing-style angle when pitching a buyer. Concrete, ROI-framed, fast yes/no decision. Use late in sequence to close.
angles.example_phrasing: Specific proposal for {talent_name}: {deliverable} + {usage_rights} + {exclusivity_terms} = {price}. {past_metric_reference} suggests {expected_outcome}.

angles.name: Strategic intro (influencer role)
angles.description: Default opener for influencer-tier contacts (CMOs etc.). Positions as 'introducing myself' without expecting them to handle the deal directly.
angles.example_phrasing: I know you sit above the day-to-day creator program — wanted to put {talent_name} on your radar in case it fits the broader strategy. Happy to be routed to whoever owns the IM budget.

angles.name: Brief routing ask (gatekeeper role)
angles.description: Default for gatekeepers (EAs, AOR account managers). Short and respectful — just asking for the right routing.
angles.example_phrasing: Quick ask — who handles creator partnerships at {target_brand}? Happy to send a brief intro about {talent_name} to them directly. Don't want to take up your time on the wrong route.

angles.name: Soft advocacy ask (champion role)
angles.description: Default for champion-classified contacts (known fans / internal advocates). Warm tone; ask for internal intro or advocacy, not a deal directly.
angles.example_phrasing: Saw your {recent_engagement_with_talent} — really appreciated it. If you ever feel like passing along {talent_name} as a creator who'd fit {target_brand}'s next campaign, would love to chat.

angles.name: Adjacent-category pitch around active exclusivity
angles.description: Talent has an active_exclusivity with a competitor in this industry but has bandwidth for a different (non-conflicting) product line at the target brand. Careful handling required.
angles.example_phrasing: Transparency: {talent_name} is currently exclusive with {exclusivity_brand} in {exclusivity_category} through {exclusivity_end_date}. But their audience is hungry for {adjacent_category} — could {target_brand}'s {different_product_line} be a fit?
angles.notes: Use carefully. Some brands appreciate the transparency; others see it as a flag. Only fire when the adjacent_category is genuinely non-competing.

angles.name: Specific past-campaign KPI
angles.description: Talent has a documented past campaign (in `data/brand_deals/{talent_id}.json`) with notable KPIs — reach, engagement, video completion, etc. Pitches the target brand with concrete numbers from a similar or competitive campaign. Email generator prefers platform_verified KPIs over self_reported when picking which figure to cite.
angles.example_phrasing: {talent_name} drove {kpi_value} {kpi_unit} for {past_brand} in {past_campaign_period} — {kpi_source_verification}. Happy to walk through the full audit.
angles.notes: When the deal's brand is a direct competitor of the target (via brand_competitors.json), this angle pairs powerfully with past_brand_direct_competitor — combined they form the strongest first-touch hook.

angles.name: Past brand renewed
angles.description: Talent has a past deal with outcome=successful_renewed — the brand chose to do a follow-on campaign. Strong social proof: 'brand X liked working with me enough to come back'. Particularly powerful when the renewing brand is in the same vertical as the target.
angles.example_phrasing: {past_brand} renewed {talent_name} for {follow_on_period} after the launch campaign — happy to walk through what worked and how it could apply to {target_brand}.

angles.name: Past campaign drove conversions / sales
angles.description: Talent has a past deal with strong bottom-funnel KPIs — conversions, link clicks, sales_attributed_usd, promo code redemptions. The headline number that buyers (especially performance-focused brands) most care about. Email generator picks the most impressive of {conversions, sales_attributed_usd, link_clicks, promo_code_redemptions} based on source confidence.
angles.example_phrasing: {talent_name}'s last campaign drove {conversion_metric_value} {conversion_metric_unit} for {past_brand} — performance audit available. Confident a similar approach lands for {target_brand}.
angles.notes: Sales/conversion numbers from brand_reported sources are the highest-trust pitch material — buyers prioritise these over engagement metrics. Email generator should flag if the only available conversion figures are self_reported (low confidence).

angles.name: Past audience overlap with similar brand's target
angles.description: Talent has a documented past campaign where `audience_overlap_with_brand_target_pct` was high (e.g. 70%+). Quantitative proof of audience-fit accuracy. Pairs with current-brand demographic angles to extend the story.
angles.example_phrasing: {talent_name}'s past audience overlap with {past_brand}'s buyer profile was {overlap_pct}% — likely even higher with {target_brand} given the demographic match.

angles.name: Past campaign beat industry benchmark
angles.description: Talent has a past campaign where `vs_industry_benchmark` shows positive (e.g. ER 2.3x category average). Strongest quantitative proof — directly contextualizes the talent's performance vs the rest of the space. NOTE: schema is in place for v0.1 but this angle fires zero times until `data/industry_kpi_benchmarks.json` ships in v2. Captured here so the trigger logic is ready to go live the moment benchmarks are added.
angles.example_phrasing: On the {past_brand} campaign, {talent_name}'s {kpi_name} was {outperformance_multiplier} the {industry} category average ({past_kpi_value} vs {benchmark_value}). Full audit shows why.
angles.notes: Dormant until v2 benchmarks ship. When live, this is the top-strength angle (0.90) — quantitative + comparative + verifiable.
